# 1 Clement Chapter 57 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 57

---

## Council Notes

**On "bending the knees of your heart" (v.1):** All agents preserve this striking image. The Greek *kampsantes ta gonata tēs kardias* is a metaphor unique to this letter (also 1 Clem 57:1). Physical prostration becomes an interior posture. All agents agree this should not be paraphrased away.

**On "small" / "humble" (v.2):** EMET: "be found small." LOGOS: "be found humble." PNEUMA: "be humble." The Greek *mikros* literally means "small/little." The contrast is "small within the flock" vs. "eminent in reputation." "Small" (EMET) preserves the economic/status contrast better than "humble," though it sounds unusual. LOGOS's "humble" is preferred for readability while retaining the theological point.

**On Proverbs 1:23–33 citation (vv.3–10):** Clement quotes LXX Proverbs at length. The voice is personified Wisdom (*sophia*), not God directly. All agents correctly treat this as a Wisdom speech. LOGOS renders it with the most precision.

**On "wronged infants" / "wronged the innocent" (v.9):** EMET: "wronged infants" (following a more literal reading of *nēpiois*). LOGOS: "wronged the innocent." The LXX Proverbs 1:32 uses *nēpioi* — literally "childlike/simple ones" (those without guile). "The innocent" (LOGOS) is the appropriate contextual rendering.

**On "ungodliness" / "impiety" (v.8):** EMET: "ungodliness." LOGOS: "impiety." PNEUMA: "godlessness." The Greek *asebeia* is a standard term. "Ungodliness" is the traditional rendering. Retained.

---

**57:1** Therefore, you who laid the foundation of the revolt, submit yourselves to the presbyters and accept correction toward repentance, bending the knees of your heart.

**57:2** Learn to be subordinate, laying aside the arrogant and proud boasting of your tongue. For it is better for you to be found humble within the flock of Christ and honorable, than to be pre-eminent in reputation and cast out from his hope.

**57:3** For thus the all-excellent Wisdom says: "Behold, I will bring forth to you the declaration of my spirit; I will teach you my word.

**57:4** Since I called and you did not obey, and I stretched forth my words and you gave no heed, and you made light of my counsels and did not attend to my reproofs,

**57:5** therefore I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice when ruin comes upon you, and when sudden confusion overtakes you, and when devastation rushes upon you like a storm, and when distress and affliction come upon you.

**57:6** For it shall be that when you call upon me I shall not hear you; evil ones shall seek me and shall not find me. For they hated wisdom and would not choose the fear of the LORD,

**57:7** neither would they attend to my counsels, but mocked my reproofs.

**57:8** Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own ungodliness.

**57:9** For because they wronged the innocent, they shall be put to death; and judgment shall destroy the ungodly.

**57:10** But the one who hears me shall dwell in confidence, and shall rest in hope undisturbed by fear of any evil."

---

*— SOPHIA*
